physical_mismatches.reason: Uniform 70ns DRAM latency assumption simplifies off-chip access time prediction; real systems have variable memory access patterns
On-chip voltage regulators (20 mV/ns switching) assumed with negligible overhead; actual power consumption and thermal effects of regulators not fully modeled in component-wise temperature feedback
32nm technology node; modern CMPs use 7nm or smaller, affecting power density and thermal behavior scaling
2D-mesh NoC with 1-cycle per-tile propagation delay; assumes uniform tiled layout without accounting for 3D stacking, interposer cooling, or heterogeneous core placement
Periodic 0.33 μs thermal stability interval assumption may not hold for transient thermal events or rapid workload phase changes

studio_assumptions: WaFFLe implementation in gem5 Ruby module with performance monitoring counters (no additional hardware cost for way-shutdown)
McPAT power model assumes uniform on-chip temperature for leakage; paper compensates with component-wise temperature from HotSpot at end of each period
HotSpot 6.0 steady-state thermal model used; no transient thermal solver or 3D heat dissipation simulation
Way-shutdown algorithm assumes clean non-MRU (CN) blocks are invalidatable without live-data loss; preliminary analysis on 9 PARSEC apps showed <2% cache sets with all-dirty blocks
FG-DVFS assumes on-chip voltage regulators present; coherence directory exploited for global isolated miss detection
All 16 cores always active (maximum workload assumption); no idle or power-gating states beyond cache-way shutdown
DVFS applied only at two V/F settings (1.12V/3.0GHz and 0.76V/1.2GHz); no intermediate frequency scaling
Intra-set cache block migration via temporary buffer preferred over off-chip writeback based on analytical cost comparison (equations 1–2)
PARSEC large input sets with 16 threads; one thread per core; no SMT or dynamic thread mapping
